text: Ignaz Alberti (11 April 1760, Vienna – 31 August 1794, Vienna) was an Austrian illustrator, engraver, and book printer who employed approximately 20 engravers in 1787, primarily for cartography and botanical publications. After his death, his widow took over the management of the printing and publication activities. In 1796, she printed and published the Vienna edition of the New Testament, which was banned by the Catholic Church and released without imprimatur. Alberti engraved and printed the frontispiece for the original libretto of Mozart's Die Zauberflöte, produced in Vienna in 1791; he was a fellow Mason in the Lodge Zur gekrönten Hoffung with Mozart, and the frontispiece, richly adorned with Masonic symbolism, was subsequently removed from all later editions of the libretto. Additionally, Mozart contributed his final three lieder (K. 596–598) to the Liedersammlung für Kinder und Kinderfreunde am Clavier, published in 1791 by Alberti—this marked the first volume in a series of four children’s song collections published in Vienna. Alberti played a key role in preparing, printing, and publishing numerous works on natural history, librettos, oratory, and other subjects. He is sometimes mistakenly identified with the engraver Ignaz Albrecht.
